sourceIdentity.title: Aspirin enhances the cytotoxic activity of bortezomib against myeloma cells via suppression of Bcl-2, survivin and phosphorylation of AKT

observations: Two human-derived myeloma cell lines MM1.S/RPMI8226, not recruited human participants/current animal experiment. N/KRas assignments reversed Abstract vs Methods, unresolved.
Experimental aspirin2.5mM plus bortezomib10nM; CCK8 at24/48/72h, apoptosis/markers48h. No clinical dose or independently verified serum-equivalence translation.
Methods ratio survival(combination)/(survivalASA*survivalBTZ);0.8<R<1.2 additive, results report additive. Greater combined effect does not become synergy. Exact conditionR not extracted.

Text48h apoptosis rates MM1.S2.73/44.8/45.4/64.3 and RPMI3.43/36.1/57.9/77.2 percent in untreated/ASA/BTZ/combination order confirmed. Figure2C three-reported-experiment summary visually distinct from representative quadrant panel values; no quadrant reconstruction.
10000 flow events per analysis not independent biological replicateN. Three experiments as reported; independent replicate status/raw data unverified. No SD/CI invented or pixel-extracted.

Figures3-5 visually show lower combination-versus-BTZ marker patterns. Figure3C bars do not support uniform BTZ-induced Ser473 increase versus untreated; candidate correctly bounds claim and retains qualification. Root sees this concern across displayed lines, not a quantitative bar reanalysis.
Changes in phosphorylation/survivin/Bcl2 are associated marker patterns, not selective binding or established causal mediation/clinical resistance reversal.

Funding NSFC81460037 and NanjingMilitary14ZD31 observed; vendors are not assumed sponsors. Current clinical efficacy, safety, trialbenefit, PK equivalence and external integrity/replication not established.
Reference29 listed as a pharmacology book review; no independently checked primary PK basis. Prior referenced in-vivo and perifosine trial results not current aspirin clinical data.
